manifest.title: Figure-Ground and Plural Projection Ontology — Framing, Provenance, and Graph-of-Graphs Knowledge
manifest.description: Graph-native ontology for reversible figure-ground assignments, plural preservation-and-loss projections, provenance-qualified convergence, complementary path and address knowledge, human-readable constellations, and durable integration across independently governed knowledge graphs.
scope: source fields, admitted fields, and explicit boundaries
inquiry-relative figure, ground, exclusion, and refiguring
projection families with preservation policies, resolution, scope, and loss profiles
addresses, paths, histories, convergence, and bounded re-entry
evidence accounts with provenance, authority, epistemic status, and account boundaries
shared identity contact without automatic equivalence
causal, structural, and explanatory projections as distinct organizations
human-readable constellations as reversible figures over retained graph ground
typed graph-of-graphs integration with namespace and conflict preservation
cross-session persistence through stable identifiers and bounded reconstruction context

nodes.label: Figure-Ground and Plural Projection Ontology
nodes.definition: A graph-native ontology for representing reversible figure-ground roles, preservation-and-loss projections, provenance-qualified convergence, plural explanatory routes, and durable graph-of-graphs knowledge.

nodes.label: Source field
nodes.definition: The richer domain from which a particular inquiry admits content.

nodes.label: Admitted field
nodes.definition: The bounded content made available to a particular inquiry before figure and ground roles are assigned.

nodes.label: Field element
nodes.definition: A distinguishable constituent admitted by a field.

nodes.label: Field relation
nodes.definition: A declared connection among field elements.

nodes.label: Field boundary
nodes.definition: The scope condition separating admitted content from content not presently admitted.

nodes.label: Retained context
nodes.definition: Admitted content kept available for interpretation even when it is not foregrounded.

nodes.label: Inquiry frame
nodes.definition: A purpose-relative arrangement of field, question, receiver position, and lens that makes an answerable inquiry possible.

nodes.label: Inquiry question
nodes.definition: The distinction or uncertainty an inquiry is organized to resolve.

nodes.label: Inquiry purpose
nodes.definition: The practical or explanatory end that guides framing and selection.

nodes.label: Receiver position
nodes.definition: The situated capacities, prior knowledge, and access conditions from which a frame is interpreted.

nodes.label: Lens
nodes.definition: A declared emphasis or interpretive criterion used within an inquiry frame.

nodes.label: Figure-ground assignment
nodes.definition: A reversible role assignment over an admitted field that marks some content as figure and retains the rest as ground.

nodes.label: Figure role
nodes.definition: The role of being presently salient to an inquiry; it is not an intrinsic property of its bearer.

nodes.label: Ground role
nodes.definition: The role of providing retained interpretive context without being presently salient; it is not absence.

nodes.label: Excluded role
nodes.definition: The role of lying outside the admitted field of a particular frame while remaining potentially available to another frame.

nodes.label: Salience assignment
nodes.definition: The graded or discrete allocation of attention within an admitted field.

nodes.label: Refiguring
nodes.definition: A change in figure-ground assignment that can reveal another coherent organization without changing the represented field.

nodes.label: Projection
nodes.definition: An operation that produces a qualified view by preserving declared structure and accepting declared loss.

nodes.label: Selector
nodes.definition: The rule or criterion by which a projection chooses what to carry forward.

nodes.label: Preservation policy
nodes.definition: A declaration of which identities, relations, distinctions, or reconstruction affordances a projection retains.

nodes.label: Loss profile
nodes.definition: A declaration of content or distinctions not carried by a projection.

nodes.label: Qualified view
nodes.definition: The result of a projection together with its scope, resolution, provenance, and loss conditions.

nodes.label: Reversible projection
nodes.definition: A projection whose retained information is sufficient for a declared bounded reconstruction, not necessarily exact inversion.

nodes.label: Resolution
nodes.definition: The granularity at which a view preserves distinctions.

nodes.label: Scope
nodes.definition: The domain and conditions within which a view or claim is licensed.

nodes.label: Projection family
nodes.definition: A set of independently useful views produced from a shared represented field under different selectors or purposes.

nodes.label: Address
nodes.definition: A compact locator for an endpoint or knowledge region that does not by itself preserve the path by which it was reached.

nodes.label: Endpoint
nodes.definition: The destination or resolved object at which a path terminates.

nodes.label: Path
nodes.definition: An ordered sequence of traversals whose history can contribute meaning beyond its endpoint.

nodes.label: Traversal
nodes.definition: One ordered step through an element, relation, transformation, or account.

nodes.label: Path history
nodes.definition: The ordered record of choices and transformations that produced an endpoint.

nodes.label: Path convergence
nodes.definition: The meeting of distinct paths at a shared endpoint or hub without erasing path-specific history.

nodes.label: Approach path
nodes.definition: A path whose ordering encodes how and why a destination was reached.

nodes.label: Re-entry path
nodes.definition: A bounded route that restores usable access to a knowledge region from a retained address and reconstruction context.

nodes.label: Represented object
nodes.definition: The object, process, or structure about which one or more evidence accounts speak.

nodes.label: Evidence account
nodes.definition: A provenance-bearing organization of evidence produced under a particular access path, authority, and purpose.

nodes.label: Evidence item
nodes.definition: A bounded observation, artifact, trace, or statement admitted by an evidence account.

nodes.label: Provenance
nodes.definition: The source, custody, transformations, and authority conditions under which knowledge was produced.

nodes.label: Source identity
nodes.definition: A stable reference to the origin responsible for an evidence item or account.

nodes.label: Authority scope
nodes.definition: The domain within which a source is licensed to make or curate a claim.

nodes.label: Epistemic status
nodes.definition: A declared classification of how a knowledge item is warranted.

nodes.label: Observation
nodes.definition: A recorded encounter under declared access and measurement conditions.

nodes.label: Assertion
nodes.definition: A claim made by an identified authority under a declared scope.

nodes.label: Inference
nodes.definition: A claim derived from other knowledge through a stated reasoning rule.

nodes.label: Evidence boundary
nodes.definition: A declared limit beyond which an evidence account does not warrant conclusions.

nodes.label: Causal lineage
nodes.definition: A claimed sequence of world-producing or state-producing dependencies supported by an evidence account.

nodes.label: Account boundary
nodes.definition: The limit of vocabulary, access, and causal visibility internal to an evidence account.

nodes.label: Identity anchor
nodes.definition: A stable reference through which independently governed accounts can be brought into contact.

nodes.label: Shared identity contact
nodes.definition: The fact that distinct accounts refer to the same anchor; contact does not by itself assert semantic or causal equivalence.

nodes.label: Convergence hub
nodes.definition: A region where multiple paths, accounts, or projections make typed contact.

nodes.label: Cross-graph alignment
nodes.definition: A scoped correspondence between independently governed graph elements.

nodes.label: Equivalence claim
nodes.definition: An explicit, separately warranted claim that two graph elements are interchangeable under a stated scope.

nodes.label: Translation bridge
nodes.definition: A typed mapping that permits movement between vocabularies while preserving source identities and declared loss.

nodes.label: Unresolved contact
nodes.definition: A shared anchor whose deeper relation has not yet been warranted.

nodes.label: Convergence pattern
nodes.definition: A recurring shape in which plural paths or accounts meet while retaining their distinct histories.

nodes.label: Explanatory projection
nodes.definition: A projection organized to answer why or how under a declared explanatory frame.

nodes.label: Causal projection
nodes.definition: A projection organized around claimed productive dependencies and temporal succession.

nodes.label: Structural projection
nodes.definition: A projection organized around identities, relations, topology, or repeated shapes.

nodes.label: Explanatory route
nodes.definition: A human-readable ordering through graph content that supports understanding without automatically asserting a world-causal edge.

nodes.label: Coherent reading
nodes.definition: An internally usable interpretation supported by a declared frame and evidence boundary.

nodes.label: Explanatory constellation
nodes.definition: A purpose-relative human-readable figure composed from selected graph elements and relations against a larger retained graph ground.

nodes.label: Narrative lineage
nodes.definition: The ordered history of selections through which an explanatory route or constellation was composed.

nodes.label: Plural account set
nodes.definition: A set of coherent accounts that may concern the same represented object while remaining unable to fully describe one another.

nodes.label: Knowledge graph
nodes.definition: A governed graph of knowledge items, relations, provenance, and boundaries.

nodes.label: Ontology graph
nodes.definition: A knowledge graph that declares the concepts and relation types by which a domain can be represented.

nodes.label: Graph of graphs
nodes.definition: A registry of independently governed graphs connected by typed, provenance-bearing bridges rather than silent union.

nodes.label: Graph namespace
nodes.definition: The identity domain within which graph identifiers are unique and governed.

nodes.label: Stable identifier
nodes.definition: A persistent identifier whose meaning and authority are governed within a namespace.

nodes.label: Bridge mapping
nodes.definition: A candidate or accepted correspondence between elements in different graph namespaces.

nodes.label: Bridge assertion
nodes.definition: A provenance-bearing statement that types, scopes, and warrants a bridge mapping.

nodes.label: Bridge conflict
nodes.definition: A recorded incompatibility among bridge assertions that must remain visible pending adjudication.

nodes.label: Versioned graph artifact
nodes.definition: A durable graph carrier with explicit identity, version, status, and lineage.

nodes.label: Queryable knowledge surface
nodes.definition: An interface that returns qualified projections while exposing provenance, scope, and loss.

nodes.label: Integration policy
nodes.definition: Rules governing graph membership, identifier boundaries, bridge admission, and conflict preservation.

nodes.label: Knowledge session
nodes.definition: A bounded episode in which a knower or process constructs, queries, or revises graph knowledge.

nodes.label: Project context
nodes.definition: A durable frame of purposes, authorities, artifacts, and vocabulary shared across multiple sessions.

nodes.label: Session context
nodes.definition: The local assumptions, active questions, and selected figures of one knowledge session.

nodes.label: Durable knowledge artifact
nodes.definition: A persistent carrier through which graph knowledge can outlive the session that produced it.

nodes.label: Re-entry address
nodes.definition: A stable locator for returning to a knowledge region without pretending to preserve the entire originating path.

nodes.label: Reconstruction context
nodes.definition: The bounded definitions, provenance, constraints, and path cues required to rebuild a usable interpretive state.

nodes.label: Bounded reconstruction
nodes.definition: Reconstruction sufficient for a declared task and scope without requiring recovery of every transient state.

nodes.label: Context capsule
nodes.definition: A compact, provenance-bearing package of address, frame, boundaries, and reconstruction cues for future re-entry.

nodes.label: Invariant remainder
nodes.definition: The minimal condition that remains stable enough to support re-entry after transient context is lost.

nodes.label: Figure and ground are frame-relative roles
nodes.definition: Being figure or ground is assigned relative to an inquiry frame and is not an intrinsic property of a field element.
nodes.formalization: For frame A over source field U: Admitted_A ⊆ U; Figure_A ∪ Ground_A = Admitted_A; Figure_A ∩ Ground_A = ∅. An element may change role under another frame B.

nodes.label: Ground is retained context, not absence
nodes.definition: Ground remains admitted and interpretively available even when it is not salient.
nodes.formalization: Ground_A(x) ⇒ x ∈ Admitted_A; therefore Ground_A(x) does not imply x is absent from U or discarded by every projection.

nodes.label: Refiguring need not change the represented field
nodes.definition: A new figure-ground assignment can expose another coherent organization while the represented field remains fixed.
nodes.formalization: It is possible that U_A = U_B while Figure_A ≠ Figure_B or Ground_A ≠ Ground_B.

nodes.label: Framing, projection, and scope-cutting are distinct operations
nodes.definition: Framing poses an inquiry, figure-ground assignment allocates salience, and projection preserves selected structure under loss; none entails the others.

nodes.label: Address and path carry complementary knowledge
nodes.definition: An address supports direct return to an endpoint, while a path can preserve the history that explains how and why it was reached.

nodes.label: A shared endpoint does not imply a shared path
nodes.definition: Distinct paths may terminate at the same endpoint while retaining different histories, purposes, and meanings.
nodes.formalization: End(p1) = End(p2) does not entail p1 = p2, History(p1) = History(p2), or Purpose(p1) = Purpose(p2).

nodes.label: Shared identity creates contact, not equivalence
nodes.definition: Reference to the same identity anchor licenses comparison but does not by itself collapse accounts, relations, or meanings.
nodes.formalization: ContactAt(a,b,h) does not entail a ≡ b.

nodes.label: One represented field may support multiple valid projections
nodes.definition: Different preservation policies and inquiry purposes can yield distinct, coherent views of the same represented field.

nodes.label: Integration must preserve provenance
nodes.definition: A graph-of-graphs must retain the source identity, authority, and transformation history of every member graph and bridge assertion.

nodes.label: Observation, assertion, and inference must not collapse
nodes.definition: Knowledge items with different warranting relations remain distinguishable even when they concern the same anchor.

nodes.label: An explanatory route is not automatically a declared world relation
nodes.definition: Ordering graph elements for understanding does not by itself assert causal, temporal, or structural adjacency in the represented field.

nodes.label: A constellation is a figure over graph ground
nodes.definition: An explanatory constellation gains coherence from a declared frame and retained graph context; it is neither the whole graph nor an arbitrary decoration.

nodes.label: Local coherence does not imply global completeness
nodes.definition: An account can coherently answer its own question while lacking the vocabulary or evidence needed to describe another coherent account.

nodes.label: Graphs integrate through typed bridges, not silent union
nodes.definition: Cross-graph integration requires explicit mappings, scope, provenance, and conflict handling while member graphs remain independently governed.

nodes.label: Identifier similarity does not establish identity
nodes.definition: Identifiers from different namespaces are not identical unless a separately warranted bridge assertion establishes a scoped relation.

nodes.label: Projection loss and re-entry conditions must be co-declared
nodes.definition: A useful durable projection states both what it omits and what bounded context permits later reconstruction or re-entry.

nodes.label: Every returned view is inquiry-relative
nodes.definition: A queryable knowledge surface returns a qualified view governed by question, scope, resolution, provenance, and loss rather than an unqualified whole.

nodes.label: Persistence requires a viable invariant remainder
nodes.definition: Knowledge survives session loss when a stable address and bounded reconstruction context retain enough structure for re-entry.

nodes.label: Coherent accounts may be mutually incomplete
nodes.definition: Distinct evidence-producing systems can produce coherent accounts of one represented object while each lacks the internal resources to explain the others.
